name: Ruben Yoon
life: “I still remember flattening an old sales receipt under a harbor chart.” On Friday, near Maré Coffee, Ruben likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I am the broker everyone bypassed. I found the original bill folded behind the depth gauge.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a striped cotton shirt and a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. Ruben has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Ruben listens with the head tilted a little to the left during a conversation.
personality: Ruben often says yes too quickly out of pride in being useful. The people closest to Ruben have learned to ask again the next morning, when the answer is more likely to account for sleep.
agenda: To recover the original boat receipt.
family: Lane Baran is Ruben’s second cousin. Ruben chooses an ordinary story to tell. Lane asks the question the rest of the family avoided. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The absent signature*, Lane says, “I delivered the letter unsigned. A week later she sent back an invitation with a harbor ticket inside.”
connections: Sam Sharp. A found invoice helps establish whether the old polishing agreement ought to survive the sale.

reactions.situation: The boat's owners give two answers about selling
reactions.response: Ruben asks both owners which decision has actually been made.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Ruben writes down the shift time accurately, then helps them explain the circumstances without having to tell the whole room.

reactions.situation: When two people ask for the same hour
reactions.response: Ruben rings both of them before quietly counting on somebody else to fill in.
